title: Tabletop KMS incident scenarios and log signatures
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight tabletop guide for running 60–90 minute simulated KMS/HSM incidents that exercise RBAC v2 misconfigurations, audit log schema completeness, evidence extraction automation, and SIEM export recipes. The goal is to produce repeatable scenarios with concrete log signatures and an evidence checklist so SRE, Security, and Product can validate detection, escalation, and rotation automation end-to-end.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Redwood-hosted KMS and customer BYOK broker flows (tenant keys + envelope keys).
- Covers HSM failover behavior (soft-fallback to software keystore), BYOK revocation, unauthorized key-export attempts, RBAC privilege escalation, and missing-audit evidence cases.
- Assumes SIEM ingest pipeline (Elastic/Chronicle/Splunk) is available and can run saved searches that return event JSON.
- Not a formal runbook for production outages; this is an exercise plan and detection playbook.

High-level roles for the tabletop:
- Incident lead: runs the scenario, times the play, coordinates notes (security ops).
- Detection owner: runs SIEM queries and notes false positives/negatives (SRE/Secops).
- KMS owner: walks through key rotation / BYOK revocation steps and confirms automation triggers (platform-engineering or keying-service).
- HSM SME: explains HSM failover and provides artifacts (appliance logs, audit export).
- Recorder: captures decisions, outstanding gaps, and action items.

RBAC v2 considerations to validate during the simulation:
- Privilege scoping: verify role-bound keys are only accessible by expected service principals.
- Delegation checks: ensure delegated roles (e.g., "key-operator") cannot perform owner-only actions (rotate/destroy).
- Emergency breakglass: simulate a breakglass user and validate additional logging & MFA challenged events are recorded.
- Test corruption: intentionally misassign a role and confirm SIEM flags unusual access patterns.

Scenario 1 — BYOK revocation after compromised tenant key (45 mins):
- Trigger: simulated compromise report (threat intel) that tenant private key material may be leaked.
- Expected timeline: 0–5m detect, 5–20m emergency revoke + roll, 20–40m verify consumer services re-encrypt or rewrap, 40–60m post-checks & evidence package.
- Detection signatures (logs you should see):
  - key_service.access_grant: {"principal":"service-X","action":"decrypt","key_id":"kt-tenant-.*","result":"success","tsa":"2024-11-06T..."}
  - key_service.policy_change: {"actor":"admin@example.com","change":"revoke-tenant-key","target":"kt-tenant-.*","request_id":"req-.*"}
  - kms.audit.hsm_fallback: {"reason":"hsm-unreachable","fallback":"software-keystore","key_ids":["kt-tenant-*"]}
- SIEM query snippets (pseudo-Elastic/SPL):
  - Elastic: event.type: "policy_change" AND key_id: /kt-tenant-/ AND change: "revoke*" | sort @timestamp
  - Splunk: index=kms_logs action=decrypt key_id=kt-tenant-* | stats count by principal, result
- Required evidence to export (audit schema fields):
  - fields: ["timestamp","request_id","actor_principal","actor_ip","action","key_id","key_version","result","change_set","hsm_node_id","audit_forwarded_to_siem"]
  - export format: newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON), compress with GZIP, sign manifest with ops-key before handing to compliance.
- Playbook steps (short):
  - 1) Set tenant key to disabled in control plane (immediate effect).
  - 2) Trigger rotation flow: allocate new envelope key and rewrap data-encryption-keys (automated or manual fallback).
  - 3) Update service configs and kick rolling restart/rotate tokens.
  - 4) Run smoke decrypt tests against representative datasets.
  - 5) Export full NDJSON of audit events covering 30m pre-compromise to 30m post-action; attach to postmortem.

Scenario 2 — Unauthorized attempt to export HSM key material (60 mins):
- Trigger: internal automation attempts to call an unsupported admin call that would result in key_export request.
- Detection signatures:
  - kms.hsm_admin_call: {"api":"ExportKey","actor":"svc-admin","result":"denied","reason":"hsm_policy_block"}
  - rbacv2.authz.evaluation: {"actor":"svc-admin","request_id":"...","policy_version":"v2.1","decision":"deny","policy_match":"no-export"}
- SIEM recipe: alert when ExportKey call + decision=deny + actor not in allowlist for 5 events in 2m => create incident.
- Evidence to capture: API trace, authorization decision blob, HSM node audit, exception stack traces for automation.

Scenario 3 — RBAC drift & sudden privilege escalation (tabletop variant, 30–45 mins):
- Trigger: periodic identity sync introduced a role-binding change (human error).
- Detection signatures:
  - iam.sync.delta: {"source":"idp-sync","change":"role-bind","affected":"svc-qa","old_roles":["key-reader"],"new_roles":["key-admin"]}
  - key_service.access: high-volume admin ops from an unexpected principal within 10 minutes.
- SIEM query: track iam.sync.delta events and correlate with admin actions within T+15m window.
- Remediation: roll back role-binding via idp snapshot and run compliance checkers.

HSM failover and evidence specifics:
- HSM event of interest: node heartbeat miss, cluster quorum lost, forced software-fallback. Logs to collect:
  - node_heartbeat: {"node":"hsm-3","missed":3}
  - hsm.cluster.event: {"event":"quorum_lost","active_nodes":1}
  - keystore.fallback: {"fallback_started":"ts","affected_keys":[],"operator":"auto"}
- Evidence automation note: ensure keystore.fallback event includes a pointer to the archived HSM audit bundle (artifact ID) so SIEM can enrich incidents with HSM-provided evidence.

Audit log schema checklist (minimum fields we require for evidence automation):
- timestamp
- request_id (uuid)
- actor_principal (email or service id)
- actor_type (user/service/automation)
- actor_ip (if available)
- action (e.g., decrypt/encrypt/rotate/disable/export)
- resource_id (key_id)
- resource_version (key_version)
- result (success/denied/error)
- detail (freeform message)
- hsm_node_id (nullable)
- policy_version (rbacv2 policy hash)
- evidence_bundle_id (if archived externally)
- forward_to_siem_status (ack/pending/fail)

Sample NDJSON event (one line):
{"timestamp":"2025-01-10T14:12:02Z","request_id":"req-2a9f","actor_principal":"svc-ingest@redwood.com","actor_type":"service","actor_ip":"10.12.3.4","action":"decrypt","resource_id":"ke-01a3","resource_version":"v3","result":"success","hsm_node_id":"hsm-2","policy_version":"rbacv2-2025-01","evidence_bundle_id":"eb-0098","forward_to_siem_status":"ack"}

SIEM enrichment and query recipes (operational tips):
- Always correlate idp-sync events with key admin actions: join on principal and a ±15 minute window.
- Saved detection: "RBAC drift -> admin action" => if match_count > 1 create ticket JIRA-SEC-DRIFT-TEMPLATE.
- Use artifact references: evidence_bundle_id should map to an objectstore path (s3://kms-audit/eb-0098.tar.gz) and be attached to the SIEM alert.

Rotation & revocation mini-playbook (ordered bullets for tabletop execution):
- Mark affected key(s) as disabled (immediate policy enforcement).
- If BYOK: revoke wrap keys in tenant KMS and notify customer onboarding ops (prebaked email template).
- Kick automated rewrap pipeline; if fails, use manual rewrap checklist (appendix).
- Verify consumers have fallback codepath (error codes) and can ack new keys.
- Update inventory: key_owner, justification, rotation_ticket_id.

Evidence packaging and handoff (for compliance):
- Package: NDJSON events + operator notes + manifests + signed checksum file.
- Retention guidance: keep raw audit events 1y hot, 7y cold for regulated customers (TBD with Legal).
- Delivery: encrypted tarball, signed manifest, intake ticket in compliance tracker.

Quick checklist for tabletop facilitators (10-min pre-run prep):
- Load synthetic audit events into a temporary index (last 90m).
- Enable saved SIEM queries and configure alert thresholds for the run.
- Create a fake breakglass principal and pre-provision a role change to flip during the run.
- Prepare a stubbed artifact store with evidence bundles (eb-0001..eb-0010).

Open questions / TODOs discovered during early runs:
- Should evidence_bundle_id be immutable and cryptographically anchored? (TODO: propose sig model)
- Policy_version granularity — do we include full policy text in the event or only a hash? (ops prefers hash, compliance asks for full text on demand)
- SLA for SIEM forward failures: who retries and how many times? (currently a manual pager).
- Automate packaging: create a lambda to gather NDJSON for a request_id window and produce signed bundles (JIRA-SEC-1987).

Appendix: manual rewrap checklist (short):
- 1) Identify affected DEKs and mapping to envelope keys.
- 2) Generate new envelope keys (via HSM or soft-key service as required).
- 3) Re-encrypt DEKs, update metadata in datastore, increment key_version.
- 4) Deploy config update to consumers with new version and flag for graceful fallback.
- 5) Run verification jobs and audit logs for each step.

Notes to self / facilitator reminders:
- Keep the run small (4–6 participants) to stay interactive.
- Capture timeline with timestamps in the recorder doc for postmortem.
- Invite product owners if the scenario touches customer-visible behavior.

References and examples:
- linked artifacts above (CONFSEC-KEYLIFE-42, JIRA-SEC-1987)
- internal hsm log format spec: hsm-logs-v2 (ask HSM SME).

End of tabletop guide.

(Quick status: draft — needs HSM SME review for accuracy of node event names and security lead sign-off for evidence retention language.)
